## Learning goals

- I will be able to calculate whether a proposed power supply is suitable for a computer or Raspberry Pi system.
- I will be able to explain which Linux skills transfer directly to a Raspberry Pi.
- I will be able to prepare a safe commissioning and recovery plan before connecting hardware.

This is important because a Raspberry Pi is both a computer and an electronic system. Reliable projects need correct power, storage, networking, software, and documentation.

## Readiness sequence

Before receiving a Raspberry Pi, complete these checkpoints:

1. Use voltage, current, and power relationships to check the required supply and connected loads.
2. Explain connector polarity and why voltage compatibility is not enough without adequate current capacity.
3. Identify the intended operating system image, storage device, hostname, accounts, and network method.
4. Plan how the image and project files will be backed up and recovered.
5. Decide which work happens locally and which work happens through SSH.
6. Prepare a small Git repository with a README, Python test program, data folder, and Quarto documentation page.
7. Draw the complete system boundary: supply, Pi, storage, network, sensors, outputs, and user.

The first Raspberry Pi lab should reuse familiar skills: boot Linux, identify hardware, update safely, clone a repository, run Python, record data, connect with SSH, use tmux, and publish results. Only then should students add sensors and control outputs.

## Evidence

Submit the power calculations, system diagram, commissioning checklist, backup plan, and repository link. Include one risk and the control that reduces it.

## Extend your learning

- Explore the official [Raspberry Pi documentation](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/).
- Compare a desktop Linux computer and Raspberry Pi using CPU architecture, RAM, storage, power, and I/O.

## Review and reflect

Which Linux skills will transfer unchanged to the Raspberry Pi? Which new risks appear when the computer is connected to physical electronics?
